name: Wabo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Yanita, Budiono, Khairiah, Tamrin & Nazarudin 2025. Phonological Sketch of the Wabo Language in Papua, in Some Efforts in Language and Literature Preservation in Indonesia, Nova Science, 217-229; no DOI/URL, chapter unobtainable.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The linguistic situation in the islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. VKI 35. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff.
sources.note: Wabo treated in sec. O (pp. 11-12: villages, dialects) and in the comparative wordlist; p. 14 states for all lists: 'Stress-accent, vowel pitch and vowel length (part of the accentual system in many of these languages) are not indicated.' Nothing specific on Wabo stress.

sources.citation: Budiono, Satwiko, Frans Asisi Datang, Sri Munawarah & Katubi. 2026. Wabo Language in Wabompi Village: Evaluation of Language Vitality and Endangerment. Theory and Practice in Language Studies 16(4): 1193-1204. DOI 10.17507/tpls.1604.15.
sources.note: Nothing; states 'The Wabo language has no language documentation material'.

sources.citation: Budiono, Satwiko, Multamia R.M.T. Lauder & Katubi. 2025. Assessing the Preservation Support of the Wabo Language as a Minority Language in Korombobi Village, Papua. Same volume, ch. 16, pp. 217-229.

van den Heuvel, Wilco. 2025. Metadocumentation for the entire collection. In van den Heuvel, W., S. Budiono & A. Schapper, Documentation and description of Wabo, an Austronesian language of Eastern Indonesia. ELAR collection wabo-vandenheuvel-0792 (ELDP SG1022), hdl:2196/91ff0638-bed9-43dc-85d1-08471f353f23.
sources.note: Nothing; 4 pp. of orthographic conventions (phonemic IPA-based transcription; {g},{ng},{y},{c},{j}; [β] written w or b) and wordlist-recording method. Collection (88 bundles: narratives, songs, elicitation, 13 village wordlists) contains no sketch grammar/phonology document as of 2026-09-17.

sources.citation: Yanita, Selly Rizki, Satwiko Budiono, Dewi Khairiah, Tamrin & Nazarudin. 2025. Phonological Sketch of the Wabo Language in Papua: A Preliminary Study. In M. Isnaeni, Katubi & M.R.M.T. Lauder (eds.), Some Efforts in Language and Literature Preservation in Indonesia: From Sumatra to Papua, ch. 18, pp. 245-258. New York: Nova Science. ISBN 979-8-89530-115-9, DOI 10.52305/VVZE0815 (Open Access).
sources.note: Nothing. The chapter (read in full, pp. 253-266) covers 15 consonant + 5 vowel phonemes, allophones [ɛ ɔ], distributions, syllable types (Table 5), vowel sequences/diphthongs, consonant clusters; conclusion mentions long vowels of undetermined status. No mention of stress, accent, tone or prosody; transcriptions carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Tamrin, Satwiko Budiono & Nazarudin. 2024. Vitalitas bahasa Wabo di Kampung Wabo. Linguistik Indonesia 42(1): 247-270. DOI 10.26499/li.v42i1.558.
sources.note: Nothing (sociolinguistic vitality; a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/stress/fonologi = 0).

sources.citation: ELAR Wabo collection 0792: audio for 'Wordlist phonetic' (wbb324) and 13 village wordlists + 'Verbal paradigm and possession of bodyparts' (open access after ELAR login).
sources.note: No published stress statement exists; the open recordings of isolated words would allow a first-hand acoustic determination of Wabo stress placement if the catalog ever admits instrumental self-measurement.

sources.citation: Tamrin & Dewi Khairiah (researchers), Absalom Kamawa (consultant). 2023. Wordlist phonetic / Kosakata fonetis (ELAR bundle wbb324, 62 pp., >1000 items Indonesian-Wabo in IPA). ELAR Wabo collection 0792.
sources.note: Primary data only; image-only scan, p. 1 inspected: IPA forms (pape, waraŋ, pitɔmey, ukabebari..) carry no stress marks. No statement.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.note: Wabo data second-hand (Silzer 1983, Anceaux 1961); ch. 4 intro: SHWNG diversity 'well represented, with the unavoidable exceptions of Kurudu and Wabo'. Nothing on Wabo stress.

sources.citation: Price, David S. & Mark Donohue. 2009. Report on the Ansus survey, West Yapen Island. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-001; Gasser, Emily. 2017. Papuan-Austronesian language contact on Yapen Island. NUSA 62; Sawaki, Yusuf. 2017. A grammar of Wooi. PhD ANU.
sources.note: Wabo only named in classification/lexicostatistics (Wabo+Kurudu group with Waropen at ~45% cognacy); nothing on Wabo stress.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco (with Satwiko Budiono & Antoinette Schapper). in prep./forthcoming. Descriptive output (sketch grammar / phonology) of ELDP project SG1022 'Documentation and description of Wabo, an Austronesian language of Eastern Indonesia' (fieldwork June 2024-May 2025; ELAR collection wabo-vandenheuvel-0792, hdl:2196/91ff0638-bed9-43dc-85d1-08471f353f23).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only professional descriptive project on Wabo (van den Heuvel wrote the 2006 Biak grammar); a phonology chapter would be the first source to state Wabo stress. Nothing deposited yet beyond metadocumentation, texts and wordlists; watch ELAR collection and the author's publications (NUSA/Wacana/APLL).

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily, Laura Arnold & David Kamholz. 2024. The languages of Halmahera and West New Guinea. In Adelaar & Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, ch. 37. OUP.

sources.note: Most recent areal survey of SHWNG phonology incl. Yapen stress systems; would confirm (second-hand) whether anything is known about East Yapen (Wabo/Kurudu) prosody. Unlikely to contain Wabo-specific data.
